title: When does pollen arrive?
hook: A flower visitor can carry more than food.

knows: Flowers have reproductive parts and can be visited by insects.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish pollen transfer to a stigma from nectar collection.

misconception: Collecting nectar and depositing pollen are necessarily the same action.
objective: Distinguish pollen transfer to a stigma from nectar collection.

claims.text: A flower visitor can carry more than food. In this schematic flower visit, which event represents pollen reaching the stigma? In the diagram, pollen carried by the visitor reaches the flower’s stigma. Pollination is pollen transfer from an anther to a stigma; nectar collection and pollination are distinct events, even when they occur during the same visit.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: A bee carries pollen to a compatible flower’s stigma. Which process is depicted? Pollen transfer to a stigma is pollination.
